Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

$$A_j = \bigcup_{d \mid j} S_d \quad \text{with the } S_d \text{ pairwise disjoint}$$

By Möbius inversion on $\sum_{d|j} |S_d| = j$, we get $|S_d| = \varphi(d)$.

This satisfies: $|A_i \cap A_j| = \left|\bigcup_{d \mid \gcd(i,j)} S_d\right| = \sum_{d \mid \gcd(i,j)} \varphi(d) = \gcd(i,j)$ ✓

For divisors of $250 = 2 \times 5^3$: $\{1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 125, 250\}$

We partition $\{1, 2, \ldots, 250\}$ into sets $S_e$ of sizes:
$$\varphi(1)=1,\; \varphi(2)=1,\; \varphi(5)=4,\; \varphi(10)=4,\; \varphi(25)=20,\; \varphi(50)=20,\; \varphi(125)=100,\; \varphi(250)=100$$

The constraint $\sum_{e: M_e \leq k} \varphi(e) \leq k$ (where $M_e = \max S_e$) forces the levels when sorted: $1, 2, 6, 10, 30, 50, 150, 250$.

**Optimal assignment** (largest elements to sets affecting fewest terms):

| Set | Size | Elements | $M_e$ |
|-----|------|----------|-------|
| $S_1$ | 1 | $\{1\}$ | 1 |
| $S_2$ | 1 | $\{2\}$ | 2 |
| $S_5$ | 4 | $\{3,4,5,6\}$ | 6 |
| $S_{10}$ | 4 | $\{7,8,9,10\}$ | 10 |
| $S_{25}$ | 20 | $\{11,\ldots,30\}$ | 30 |
| $S_{50}$ | 20 | $\{31,\ldots,50\}$ | 50 |
| $S_{125}$ | 100 | $\{51,\ldots,150\}$ | 150 |
| $S_{250}$ | 100 | $\{151,\ldots,250\}$ | 250 |

## Computing the Sum

$$a_1 = \max S_1 = 1$$
$$a_2 = \max(S_1 \cup S_2) = 2$$
$$a_5 = \max(S_1 \cup S_5) = 6$$
$$a_{10} = \max(S_1 \cup S_2 \cup S_5 \cup S_{10}) = 10$$
$$a_{25} = \max(S_1 \cup S_5 \cup S_{25}) = 30$$
$$a_{50} = \max(S_1 \cup S_2 \cup S_5 \cup S_{10} \cup S_{25} \cup S_{50}) = 50$$
$$a_{125} = \max(S_1 \cup S_5 \cup S_{25} \cup S_{125}) = 150$$
$$a_{250} = 250$$

**Total:** $1 + 2 + 6 + 10 + 30 + 50 + 150 + 250 = 499$

I verified this is optimal by checking that any attempt to reduce a term (e.g., making $a_{125} < 150$) forces other terms to increase by more than the savings, due to the disjointness constraint requiring the cumulative capacity condition.

$$\boxed{499}$$
